- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a bias toward higher values.
- After sharp spikes in true outcomes (e.g., 87.82, 88.99, 91.54), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct, indicating lag in adjusting to volatility.
- When sentiment history is neutral (all 0.00), model lacks behavioral cues to adjust, leading to persistent overconfidence in upward trends.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model fails to anticipate sharp declines after peaks, especially in mid-to-late forecast horizon.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually flatten — suggesting model underestimates volatility decay or overfits recent trends.
- No sentiment-driven correction observed — model ignores sentiment history, even when it’s zero, implying a need to treat neutral sentiment as a signal to reduce confidence or adjust slope.
